name: usbredir
why: A protocol for tunnelling raw USB traffic over a network, a rarely examined door into how devices get redirected.

brief.what_it_is: usbredir is a USB traffic redirection library, described on its GitLab page as "usbredir libraries and utilities". The formula lists one executable, usbredirect. The homepage I reached is the SPICE project's page, which says SPICE lets you share USB devices with virtual machines, and it names usbredir nowhere. I could not read the usbredir README, so I cannot confirm from a source here what it takes in or puts out. The scout note describes it as a protocol for tunnelling raw USB traffic over a network; that is unverified.
brief.why_it_exists: The SPICE homepage frames the wider project as providing "a complete open source solution for remote access to virtual machines in a seamless way so you can play videos, record audio, share usb devices and share folders without complications." I did not get a usbredir-specific statement of purpose.
brief.install_notes: Nothing verified beyond the formula's brew install. I did not see build, dependency, or first-run instructions because the README did not load.
brief.standout: The scout note calls it a rarely examined route by which USB devices get redirected into remote machines. I could not verify the mechanism or any detail that would make it stand out from similar tools.
brief.status: unknown. The GitLab project page shows a creation date of May 05, 2018 but no last release or last commit date. The README page returned only a spam-restriction admin notice and no content. The project carries a GNU GPL v2.0 or later license label.
brief.caveats: The homepage fetched is the SPICE project page, not a usbredir page. The usbredir README did not load; the GitLab page showed only an admin notice about spam restrictions on new accounts. Nothing about usbredir's protocol, commands, platforms, or build requirements was verified. The usbredirect executable's usage was not seen.
quotes: provide a complete open source solution for remote access to virtual machines in a seamless way so you can play videos, record audio, share usb devices and share folders without complications.
